subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for September 24, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

script.heading: Story 1 - Prophylactic vs Therapeutic Anticoagulation in Hospitalized Pa
sentences: Story 1 is about Prophylactic vs Therapeutic Anticoagulation in Hospitalized Patients With COVID-19: A Randomized Clinical Trial..
This is a randomized / clinical trial from JAMA network open.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in patients with a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19 who were hospitalized in an intensive care unit or non-intensive care ward at 1 of 10 university hospitals in Germany from November 12, 202, how should we interpret Prophylactic compared with Therapeutic Anticoagulation in Hospitalized Patients With COVID-19: A Randomized Clinical Trial?
A total of 139 patients (mean [SD] age, 58.4 [13.7] years; 93 [67%] male and 46 [33%] female) were included in the study.
Of these, 71 patients (51%) were randomized to prophylactic anticoagulation group, whereas 68 (49%) were randomized to the therapeutic anticoagulation group.

The primary outcome occurred in 14 of 67 patients (21%; 2.31 incidence per patient-year) assigned to therapeutic anticoagulation and 20 of 70 (29%; 3.37 incidence per patient-year) assigned to prophylactic anticoagulation (primary end point assessment not available for 2 patients) with primary end point assessment (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.38-1.48; P = .40).
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Use this for journal club before practice change; decide whether the measured outcome is important enough for bedside decisions.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

sentences: Story 3 is about Probiotics and Risk of Death, Necrotizing Enterocolitis, and Sepsis in Very Preterm Infants..

Among 4695 infants (mean [SD] gestational age, 30.2 [1.1] weeks; 2550 male [54.3%]), probiotic exposure increased from 0% before the national recommendation in 2020 to 16.9% in 2020 and a mean (SD) of 64.8% (4.7%) in 2021 to 2024.

script.heading: Outro

articles.title: Prophylactic vs Therapeutic Anticoagulation in Hospitalized Patients With COVID-19: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: This prospective, assessor-blinded, multicenter, parallel-group (1:1), placebo-controlled, superiority randomized clinical trial (HERO-19) assessed patients with a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19 who were hospitalized in an intensive care unit or non-intensive care ward at 1 of 10 university hospitals in Germany from November 12, 2020, to January 15, 2023. Patients were treated for 42 days. The primary end point was time to the first occurrence of all-cause mortality and/or venous thromboembolism and/or arterial thromboembolism within up to 42 days. Potential thromboembolic events were assessed by duplex ultrasonography of arms and legs at day 14 or discharge and day 42. A total of 139 patients (mean [SD] age, 58.4 [13.7] years; 93 [67%] male and 46 [33%] female) were included in the study.

articles.title: Probiotics and Risk of Death, Necrotizing Enterocolitis, and Sepsis in Very Preterm Infants.
articles.summary: In 2020, the Swedish Neonatal Society issued a national recommendation to supplement very preterm infants (28 weeks 0 days' to 31 weeks 6 days' gestation) with probiotics. To investigate whether probiotic supplementation was associated with risk of death, necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), and/or culture-proven sepsis in infants born very preterm. Live-born, very preterm infants, excluding those who died within the first 3 days of life or due to congenital or chromosomal abnormalities, were included. Composites of death and/or NEC (Bell stage 2-3), death and/or surgical NEC (Bell stage 3), and death and/or culture-proven sepsis were assessed. Among 4695 infants (mean [SD] gestational age, 30.2 [1.1] weeks; 2550 male [54.3%]), probiotic exposure increased from 0% before the national recommendation in 2020 to 16.9% in 2020 and a mean (SD) of 64.8% (4.7%) in 2021 to 2024.

Probiotic supplementation vs no supplementation was associated with lower risk of death and/or NEC (rate, 0.8% vs 3.4%; adjusted relative risk [ARR], 0.28 [95% CI, 0.14-0.56]).
